def solve():
    # Board size
    N, M = 40, 60
    total_squares = N * M
    # Knights' graph is bipartite. Let B and W be the two partitions.
    # |B| = |W| = total_squares / 2 = 1200.
    # If Horst only picks from B, then N(K) is in W.
    # In each round:
    # 1. Horst picks s_k from B \ (K U Q).
    # 2. Queenie picks s_q from S \ (K U Q).
    # The game ends when Horst cannot pick s_k or Queenie cannot pick s_q.
    # Horst cannot pick s_k if (S \ (K U Q)) is a subset of N(K).
    # If Horst only picks from B, (S \ (K U Q)) = (B \ (K U Q)) U (W \ (K U Q)).
    # For (S \ (K U Q)) to be a subset of N(K) (which is in W), we must have B \ (K U Q) = empty.
    # If the game ends because B \ (K U Q) = empty:
    # |K| + |Q \cap B| = |B| = 1200.
    # Since |Q| <= |K| (Queenie moves after Horst), |Q \cap B| <= |K|.
    # So |K| + |K| >= 1200 => |K| >= 600.
    # If the game ends because Queenie cannot move:
    # S \ (K U Q) = empty => |K| + |Q| = 2400.
    # Since |Q| <= |K|, 2|K| >= 2400 => |K| >= 1200.
    # In both cases, |K| >= 600.
    # Now, can Queenie force |K| = 600?
    # If Horst's strategy is to only pick from B, then Queenie's strategy to minimize |K|
    # is to pick from B as well.
    # In each round, 2 squares in B are filled.
    # After 600 rounds, B is completely filled. |K| = 600 and |Q \cap B| = 600.
    # Now it's Horst's turn. He needs to pick s in S \ (K U Q) = W \ Q.
    # Since Q \subseteq B, W \ Q = W.
    # He can pick s in W if it's not attacked by any knight in K.
    # If Queenie can force Horst to pick K such that N(K) = W, she might end the game.
    # But Horst picks K, so he can try to avoid N(K) = W.
    # Regardless, he already has 600 knights.
    return 600

print(solve())
